# Document: addMatchingNotification

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809749-addmatchingnotification
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809749-addmatchingnotification

# addMatchingNotification

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Adds a persistant notification handler to be notified of IOService events.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static IONotifier * addMatchingNotification( 
 const OSSymbol *type,
 OSDictionary *matching, 
 IOServiceMatchingNotificationHandler handler, 
 void *target,
 void *ref = 0, 
 SInt32 priority = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `type`: An OSSymbol identifying the type of notification and IOService state:

  ` gIOPublishNotification` Delivered when an IOService object is registered.

  ` gIOFirstPublishNotification` Delivered when an IOService object is registered, but only once per IOService instance. Some IOService objects may be reregistered when their state is changed.

  ` gIOMatchedNotification` Delivered when an IOService object has been matched with all client drivers, and they have been probed and started.

  ` gIOFirstMatchNotification` Delivered when an IOService object has been matched with all client drivers, but only once per IOService instance. Some IOService objects may be reregistered when their state is changed.

  ` gIOTerminatedNotification` Delivered after an IOService object has been terminated, during its finalize stage.
- `matching`: A matching dictionary to restrict notifications to only matching IOService objects. The dictionary is retained while the notification is installed. (Differs from addNotification).
- `handler`: A C function callback to deliver notifications.
- `target`: An instance reference for the callback's use.
- `ref`: A reference constant for the callback's use.
- `priority`: A constant ordering all notifications of a each type.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An instance of an IONotifier object that can be used to control or destroy the notification request.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

IOService will deliver notifications of changes in state of an IOService object to registered clients. The type of notification is specified by a symbol, for example `gIOMatchedNotification` or `gIOTerminatedNotification`, and notifications will only include IOService objects that match the supplied matching dictionary. Notifications are ordered by a priority set with `addNotification`. When the notification is installed, its handler will be called with each of any currently existing IOService objects that are in the correct state (eg. registered) and match the supplied matching dictionary, avoiding races between finding preexisting and new IOService events. The notification request is identified by an instance of an IONotifier object, through which it can be enabled, disabled, or removed. `addMatchingNotification` does not consume a reference on the matching dictionary when the notification is removed, unlike addNotification.

# addNotification

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Deprecated use addMatchingNotification(). Adds a persistant notification handler to be notified of IOService events.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static IONotifier * addNotification( 
 const OSSymbol *type,
 OSDictionary *matching, 
 IOServiceNotificationHandler handler, 
 void *target,
 void *ref = 0, 
 SInt32 priority = 0 ) __attribute__((deprecated)); 
```

## Parameters

- `type`: An OSSymbol identifying the type of notification and IOService state:

  ` gIOPublishNotification` Delivered when an IOService object is registered.

  ` gIOFirstPublishNotification` Delivered when an IOService object is registered, but only once per IOService instance. Some IOService objects may be reregistered when their state is changed.

  ` gIOMatchedNotification` Delivered when an IOService object has been matched with all client drivers, and they have been probed and started.

  ` gIOFirstMatchNotification` Delivered when an IOService object has been matched with all client drivers, but only once per IOService instance. Some IOService objects may be reregistered when their state is changed.

  ` gIOTerminatedNotification` Delivered after an IOService object has been terminated, during its finalize stage.
- `matching`: A matching dictionary to restrict notifications to only matching IOService objects. The dictionary will be released when the notification is removed, consuming the passed-in reference.
- `handler`: A C function callback to deliver notifications.
- `target`: An instance reference for the callback's use.
- `ref`: A reference constant for the callback's use.
- `priority`: A constant ordering all notifications of a each type.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An instance of an IONotifier object that can be used to control or destroy the notification request.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The type of notification is specified by a symbol, for example `gIOMatchedNotification` or `gIOTerminatedNotification`, and notifications will only include IOService objects that match the supplied matching dictionary. # Document: addPowerChild

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809766-addpowerchild
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809766-addpowerchild

# addPowerChild

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Informs a driver that it has a new child.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn addPowerChild(
 IOService *theChild ); 
```

## Parameters

- `theChild`: A pointer to the child IOService object.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The Platform Expert uses this method to call a driver and introduce it to a new child. This call is handled internally by power management. It is not intended to be overridden or called by drivers.

# adjustBusy

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Adjusts the `busyState` of an IOService object.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void adjustBusy(
 SInt32delta ); 
```

## Parameters

- `delta`: The delta to be applied to the IOService object's `busyState`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Applies a delta to an IOService object's `busyState`. A change in the `busyState` to or from zero will change the IOService object's provider's `busyState` by one (in the same direction).

# Document: attach

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809786-attach
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809786-attach

# attach

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Attaches an IOService client to a provider in the I/O Registry.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool attach(
 IOService *provider ); 
```

## Parameters

- `provider`: The IOService object which will serve as this object's provider.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`false` if the provider is inactive or on a resource failure; otherwise `true`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This function called in an IOService client enters the client into the I/O Registry as a child of the provider in the service plane. The provider must be active or the attach will fail. Multiple attach calls to the same provider are no-ops and return success. A client may be attached to multiple providers. Entering an object into the I/O Registry retains both the client and provider until they are detached.

# Document: callPlatformFunction

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809795-callplatformfunction
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809795-callplatformfunction

# callPlatformFunction

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Calls the platform function with the given name.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn callPlatformFunction(
 const OSSymbol *functionName, 
 bool waitForFunction, 
 void *param1,
 void *param2, 
 void *param3,
 void *param4 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `functionName`: Name of the function to be called. When `functionName` is a C string, `callPlatformFunction` converts the C string to an OSSymbol and calls the OSSymbol version of `callPlatformFunction`. This process can block and should not be used from an interrupt context.
- `waitForFunction`: If `true`, `callPlatformFunction` will not return until the function has been called.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An IOReturn code; `kIOReturnSuccess` if the function was successfully executed, `kIOReturnUnsupported` if a service to execute the function could not be found. Other return codes may be returned by the function.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The platform expert or other drivers may implement various functions to control hardware features. `callPlatformFunction` allows any IOService object to access these functions. Normally `callPlatformFunction` is called on a service's provider. The provider services the request or passes it to its provider. The system's IOPlatformExpert subclass catches functions it knows about and redirects them into other parts of the service plane. If the IOPlatformExpert subclass cannot execute the function, the base class is called. The IOPlatformExpert base class attempts to find a service to execute the function by looking up the function name in an IOResources name space. A service may publish a service using `publishResource(functionName, this)`. If no service can be found to execute the function an error is returned.

# causeInterrupt

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Causes a device interrupt to occur.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn causeInterrupt(
 intsource); 
```

## Parameters

- `source`: The index of the interrupt source in the device.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An IOReturn code (`kIOReturnNoInterrupt` is returned if the source is not valid).

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Emulates a hardware interrupt, to be called from task level.

# Document: changePowerStateTo

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809809-changepowerstateto
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809809-changepowerstateto

# changePowerStateTo

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Sets a driver's power state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IOReturn changePowerStateTo(
 unsigned longordinal ); 
```

## Parameters

- `ordinal`: The number of the desired power state in the power state array.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A return code that can be ignored by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This function is one of several that are used to set a driver's power state. In most circumstances, however, you should call changePowerStateToPriv instead. Calls to `changePowerStateTo`, `changePowerStateToPriv`, and a driver's power children all affect the power state of a driver. For legacy design reasons, they have overlapping functionality. Although you should call `changePowerStateToPriv` to change your device's power state, you might need to call `changePowerStateTo` in the following circumstances:

- If a driver will be using `changePowerStateToPriv` to change its power state, it should call `changePowerStateTo(0)` in its `start` routine to eliminate the influence `changePowerStateTo` has on power state calculations.
- Call `changePowerStateTo` in conjunction with setIdleTimerPeriod and activityTickle to idle a driver into a low power state. For a driver with 3 power states, for example, `changePowerStateTo(1)` sets a minimum level of power state 1, such that the idle timer period may not set your device's power any lower than state 1.

# Document: changePowerStateToPriv

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809819-changepowerstatetopriv
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809819-changepowerstatetopriv

# changePowerStateToPriv

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Tells a driver's superclass to change the power state of its device.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IOReturn changePowerStateToPriv(
 unsigned longordinal ); 
```

## Parameters

- `ordinal`: The number of the desired power state in the power state array.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A return code that can be ignored by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A driver uses this method to tell its superclass to change the power state of the device. This is the recommended way to change the power state of a device. Three things affect driver power state: changePowerStateTo, `changePowerStateToPriv`, and the desires of the driver's power plane children. Power management puts the device into the maximum state governed by those three entities. Drivers may eliminate the influence of the `changePowerStateTo` method on power state one of two ways. See powerOverrideOnPriv to ignore the method's influence, or call `changePowerStateTo(0)` in the driver's `start` routine to remove the `changePowerStateTo` method's power request.

# Document: close

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809831-close
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809831-close

# close

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Releases active access to a provider.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void close(
 IOService *forClient, 
 IOOptionBits options = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `forClient`: Designates the client of the provider requesting the close.
- `options`: Options available for the close. The provider family may implement options for close; IOService defines none.
- `arg`: Family specific arguments which are ignored by IOService.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

IOService provides generic open and close semantics to track clients of a provider that have established an active datapath. The use of open and `close`, and rules regarding ownership are family defined, and defined by the handleOpen and handleClose methods in the provider.

# Document: command_received

# command_received

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void command_received(
 void *,
 void *,
 void *,
 void *); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This call is handled internally by power management. It is not intended to be overridden or called by drivers.

# compareProperties

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Compares a set of properties in a matching dictionary with an IOService object's property table.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool compareProperties(
 OSDictionary *matching, 
 OSCollection *keys ); 
```

## Parameters

- `matching`: The matching dictionary, which must be non-zero.
- `keys`: A collection (eg. OSSet, OSArray, OSDictionary) which should contain OSStrings (or OSSymbols) that specify the property keys to be compared.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Success if `compareProperty` returns `true` for each key in the collection; otherwise failure.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This is a helper function to aid in implementing matchPropertyTable. A collection of dictionary keys specifies properties in a matching dictionary to be compared, with `compareProperty`, with an IOService object's property table, if `compareProperty` returns `true` for each key, success is returned; otherwise failure.

# Document: compareProperty(OSDictionary *, const char *)

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809855-compareproperty
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809855-compareproperty

# compareProperty(OSDictionary \*, const char \*)

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Compares a property in a matching dictionary with an IOService object's property table.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool compareProperty(
 OSDictionary *matching, 
 const char *key ); 
```

## Parameters

- `matching`: The matching dictionary, which must be non-zero.
- `key`: The dictionary key specifying the property to be compared, as a C string.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if the property does not exist in the matching table. If the property exists in the matching dictionary but not the IOService property table, failure is returned. Otherwise the result of calling the property from the matching dictionary's `isEqualTo` method with the IOService property as an argument is returned.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This is a helper function to aid in implementing matchPropertyTable. If the property specified by `key` exists in the matching dictionary, it is compared with a property of the same name in the IOService object's property table. The comparison is performed with the `isEqualTo` method. If the property does not exist in the matching table, success is returned. If the property exists in the matching dictionary but not the IOService property table, failure is returned.

# Document: compareProperty(OSDictionary *, const OSString *)

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809861-compareproperty
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809861-compareproperty

# compareProperty(OSDictionary \*, const OSString \*)

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Compares a property in a matching dictionary with an IOService object's property table.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool compareProperty(
 OSDictionary *matching, 
 const OSString *key ); 
```

## Parameters

- `matching`: The matching dictionary, which must be non-zero.
- `key`: The dictionary key specifying the property to be compared, as an OSString (which includes OSSymbol).

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if the property does not exist in the matching table. If the property exists in the matching dictionary but not the IOService property table, failure is returned. Otherwise the result of calling the property from the matching dictionary's `isEqualTo` method with the IOService property as an argument is returned.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This is a helper function to aid in implementing matchPropertyTable. If the property specified by `key` exists in the matching dictionary, it is compared with a property of the same name in the IOService object's property table. The comparison is performed with the `isEqualTo` method. If the property does not exist in the matching table, success is returned. If the property exists in the matching dictionary but not the IOService property table, failure is returned.

# copyClientWithCategory

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOService * copyClientWithCategory(
 const OSSymbol *category ); 
```

## Parameters

- `category`: An OSSymbol corresponding to an IOMatchCategory matching property.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Returns a reference to the IOService child with the given category. The result should be released by the caller.

# copyMatchingService

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Finds one of the current published IOService objects matching a matching dictionary.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static IOService * copyMatchingService(
 OSDictionary *matching ); 
```

## Parameters

- `matching`: The matching dictionary describing the desired IOService object.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The IOService object or NULL. To be released by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Provides a method to find one member of the set of published IOService objects matching the supplied matching dictionary.

# currentCapability

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Finds out the capability of a device's current power state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IOPMPowerFlags currentCapability(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A copy of the `capabilityFlags` field for the current power state in the power state array.

# Document: currentPowerConsumption

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809899-currentpowerconsumption
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809899-currentpowerconsumption

# currentPowerConsumption

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Finds out the current power consumption of a device.

## Declaration

```objectivec
unsigned long currentPowerConsumption(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A copy of the `staticPower` field for the current power state in the power state array.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Most macOS power managed drivers do not report their power consumption via the `staticPower` field. Thus this call will not accurately reflect power consumption for most drivers.

## See Also

# Document: deRegisterInterestedDriver

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809905-deregisterinteresteddriver
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809905-deregisterinteresteddriver

# deRegisterInterestedDriver

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

De-registers power state interest from a previous call to `registerInterestedDriver`.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IOReturn deRegisterInterestedDriver(
 IOService *theDriver ); 
```

## Parameters

- `theDriver`: The interested driver previously passed into registerInterestedDriver.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A return code that can be ignored by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The retain from `registerInterestedDriver` is released. This method is synchronous against any `powerStateWillChangeTo` or `powerStateDidChangeTo` call targeting the interested driver, so when this method returns it is guaranteed those interest handlers will not be entered. Most drivers do not need to override `deRegisterInterestedDriver`.

# Document: detach

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809913-detach
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809913-detach

# detach

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Detaches an IOService client from a provider in the I/O Registry.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void detach(
 IOService *provider ); 
```

## Parameters

- `provider`: The IOService object to detach from.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This function called in an IOService client removes the client as a child of the provider in the service plane of the I/O Registry. If the provider is not a parent of the client this is a no-op, otherwise the I/O Registry releases both the client and provider.

# Document: didTerminate

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809918-didterminate
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809918-didterminate

# didTerminate

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Passes a termination up the stack.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool didTerminate(
 IOService *provider,
 IOOptionBitsoptions,
 bool *defer ); 
```

## Parameters

- `provider`: The terminated provider of this object.
- `options`: Options originally passed to terminate.
- `defer`: If there is pending I/O that requires this object to persist, and the provider is not opened by this object set `defer` to `true` and call the `IOService::didTerminate()` implementation when the I/O completes. Otherwise, leave `defer` set to its default value of `false`.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Notification that a provider has been terminated, sent after recursing up the stack, in leaf-to-root order.

# Document: didYouWakeSystem

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809924-didyouwakesystem
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809924-didyouwakesystem

# didYouWakeSystem

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Asks a driver if its device is the one that just woke the system from sleep.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool didYouWakeSystem(
 void ) __attribute__((deprecated)); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if the driver's device woke the system and `false` otherwise.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Power management calls a power managed driver with this method to ask if its device is the one that just woke the system from sleep. If a device is capable of waking the system from sleep, its driver should implement `didYouWakeSystem` and return `true` if its device was responsible for waking the system.

# Document: disableInterrupt

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809929-disableinterrupt
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809929-disableinterrupt

# disableInterrupt

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Synchronously disables a device interrupt.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn disableInterrupt(
 intsource); 
```

## Parameters

- `source`: The index of the interrupt source in the device.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An IOReturn code (`kIOReturnNoInterrupt` is returned if the source is not valid).

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

If the interrupt routine is running, the call will block until the routine completes. It is the caller's responsiblity to keep track of the enable state of the interrupt source.

# enableInterrupt

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Enables a device interrupt.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn enableInterrupt(
 intsource); 
```

## Parameters

- `source`: The index of the interrupt source in the device.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An IOReturn code (`kIOReturnNoInterrupt` is returned if the source is not valid).

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

It is the caller's responsiblity to keep track of the enable state of the interrupt source.

# Document: errnoFromReturn

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809942-errnofromreturn
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809942-errnofromreturn

# errnoFromReturn

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Translates an IOReturn code to a BSD `errno`.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual int errnoFromReturn(
 IOReturnrtn ); 
```

## Parameters

- `rtn`: The IOReturn code.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The BSD `errno` or `EIO` if unknown.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

BSD defines its own return codes for its functions in `sys/errno.h`, and I/O Kit families may need to supply compliant results in BSD shims. Results are available for the standard return codes in `IOReturn.h` in IOService, while subclasses may implement this method to interpret family dependent return codes.

# Document: finalize

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809948-finalize
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809948-finalize

# finalize

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Finalizes the destruction of an IOService object.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool finalize(
 IOOptionBitsoptions ); 
```

## Parameters

- `options`: The options passed to the terminate method of the IOService object are passed on to `finalize`.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The `finalize` method is called in an inactive (ie. terminated) IOService object after the last client has detached. IOService's implementation will call stop, close, and detach on each provider. When `finalize` returns, the object's retain count will have no references generated by IOService's registration process.

# Document: getAggressiveness

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809962-getaggressiveness
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809962-getaggressiveness

# getAggressiveness

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns the current aggressiveness value for the given type.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn getAggressiveness( 
 unsigned longtype, 
 unsigned long *currentLevel ); 
```

## Parameters

- `type`: The aggressiveness factor to query.
- `currentLevel`: Upon successful return, contains the value of aggressiveness factor `type`.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`kIOReturnSuccess` upon success; an I/O Kit error code otherwise.

# Document: getBusyState

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809968-getbusystate
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809968-getbusystate

# getBusyState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns the `busyState` of an IOService object.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual UInt32 getBusyState(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The `busyState` value.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Many activities in IOService are asynchronous. When registration, matching, or termination is in progress on an IOService object, its `busyState` is increased by one. Change in `busyState` to or from zero also changes the IOService object's provider's `busyState` by one, which means that an IOService object is marked busy when any of the above activities is ocurring on it or any of its clients.

# Document: getClient

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809973-getclient
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809973-getclient

# getClient

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns an IOService object's primary client.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOService * getClient(
 void ) const; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The first client of the provider, or zero if the IOService object is not attached into the I/O Registry. The client is retained while it is attached, and should not be released by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This function called in an IOService provider will return the first client to attach to it. For IOService objects which have only only one client, this may be a useful simplification.

# getClientIterator

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns an iterator over an IOService object's clients.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual OSIterator * getClientIterator(
 void ) const; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An iterator over the clients of the provider, or zero if there is a resource failure. The iterator must be released when the iteration is finished. All objects returned by the iteration are retained while the iterator is valid, though they may no longer be attached during the iteration.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

For IOService objects that may have multiple clients, this method supplies an iterator over a provider's clients.

# getDeviceMemory

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns the array of IODeviceMemory objects representing a device's memory mapped ranges.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual OSArray * getDeviceMemory(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An OSArray of IODeviceMemory objects, or zero if none are available. The array is retained by the provider, so is valid while attached.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method returns an array of IODeviceMemory objects representing the physical memory ranges allocated to a memory mapped device.

# getDeviceMemoryCount

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns a count of the physical memory ranges available for a device.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOItemCount getDeviceMemoryCount(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An integer count of the number of ranges available.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method returns the count of physical memory ranges, each represented by an IODeviceMemory instance, that have been allocated for a memory mapped device.

# Document: getDeviceMemoryWithIndex

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809999-getdevicememorywithindex
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1809999-getdevicememorywithindex

# getDeviceMemoryWithIndex

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns an instance of IODeviceMemory representing one of a device's memory mapped ranges.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IODeviceMemory * getDeviceMemoryWithIndex(
 unsigned intindex ); 
```

## Parameters

- `index`: An index into the array of ranges assigned to the device.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A pointer to an instance of IODeviceMemory, or zero if the index is beyond the count available. The IODeviceMemory is retained by the provider, so is valid while attached, or while any mappings to it exist. It should not be released by the caller. See also mapDeviceMemoryWithIndex, which creates a device memory mapping.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method returns a pointer to an instance of IODeviceMemory for the physical memory range at the given index for a memory mapped device.

# Document: getInterruptType

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810004-getinterrupttype
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810004-getinterrupttype

# getInterruptType

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns the type of interrupt used for a device supplying hardware interrupts.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn getInterruptType(
 intsource,
 int *interruptType); 
```

## Parameters

- `source`: The index of the interrupt source in the device.
- `interruptType`: The interrupt type for the interrupt source will be stored here by `getInterruptType`.

  ` kIOInterruptTypeEdge` will be returned for edge-trigggered sources.

  `kIOInterruptTypeLevel` will be returned for level-trigggered sources.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An IOReturn code (`kIOReturnNoInterrupt` is returned if the source is not valid).

# Document: getMatchingServices

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810011-getmatchingservices
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810011-getmatchingservices

# getMatchingServices

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Finds the set of current published IOService objects matching a matching dictionary.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static OSIterator * getMatchingServices(
 OSDictionary *matching ); 
```

## Parameters

- `matching`: The matching dictionary describing the desired IOService objects.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An instance of an iterator over a set of IOService objects. To be released by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Provides a method of finding the current set of published IOService objects matching the supplied matching dictionary.

# Document: getOpenClientIterator

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810018-getopenclientiterator
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810018-getopenclientiterator

# getOpenClientIterator

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns an iterator over a provider's clients that currently have opened the provider.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual OSIterator * getOpenClientIterator(
 void ) const; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An iterator over the clients that have opened the provider, or zero if there is a resource failure. The iterator must be released when the iteration is finished. All objects returned by the iteration are retained while the iterator is valid, and the current entry in the iteration is locked with `lockForArbitration`, protecting it from state changes.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

For IOService objects that may have multiple clients, this method supplies an iterator over a provider's clients, locking each in turn with lockForArbitration and returning those that have opened the provider.

# Document: getOpenProviderIterator

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810027-getopenprovideriterator
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810027-getopenprovideriterator

# getOpenProviderIterator

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns an iterator over an client's providers that are currently opened by the client.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual OSIterator * getOpenProviderIterator(
 void ) const; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An iterator over the providers the client has open, or zero if there is a resource failure. The iterator must be released when the iteration is finished. All objects returned by the iteration are retained while the iterator is valid, and the current entry in the iteration is locked with `lockForArbitration`, protecting it from state changes.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

For those few IOService objects that obtain service from multiple providers, this method supplies an iterator over a client's providers, locking each in turn with lockForArbitration and returning those that have been opened by the client.

# getPMRootDomain

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns a pointer to the power management root domain instance for the computer.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static class IOPMrootDomain * getPMRootDomain(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A pointer to the power management root domain instance. It should not be released by the caller.

## Overview

This method provides an accessor to the power management root domain instance for the computer.

# Document: getPMworkloop

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810059-getpmworkloop
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810059-getpmworkloop

# getPMworkloop

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns a pointer to the system-wide power management work loop.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOWorkLoop * getPMworkloop(
 void ) __attribute__((deprecated)); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Most drivers should create their own work loops to synchronize their code; drivers should not run arbitrary code on the power management work loop.

# Document: getPowerState

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810074-getpowerstate
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810074-getpowerstate

# getPowerState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Determines a device's power state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
UInt32 getPowerState(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The current power state's index into the device's power state array.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A device's "current power state" is updated at the end of each power state transition (e.g. transition from state 1 to state 0, or state 0 to state 2). This transition includes the time spent powering on or off any power plane children. Thus, if a child calls `getPowerState` on its power parent during system wake from sleep, the call will return the index to the device's off state rather than its on state.

# Document: getProvider

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810088-getprovider
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810088-getprovider

# getProvider

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns an IOService object's primary provider.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOService * getProvider(
 void ) const; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The first provider of the client, or zero if the IOService object is not attached into the I/O Registry. The provider is retained while the client is attached, and should not be released by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This function called in an IOService client will return the provider to which it was first attached. Because the majority of IOService objects have only one provider, this is a useful simplification and also supports caching of the provider when the I/O Registry is unchanged.

Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810097-getprovideriterator

# getProviderIterator

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns an iterator over an IOService object's providers.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual OSIterator * getProviderIterator(
 void ) const; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An iterator over the providers of the client, or zero if there is a resource failure. The iterator must be released when the iteration is finished. All objects returned by the iteration are retained while the iterator is valid, though they may no longer be attached during the iteration.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

For those few IOService objects that obtain service from multiple providers, this method supplies an iterator over a client's providers.

# Document: getResources

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810107-getresources
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810107-getresources

# getResources

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Allocates any needed resources for a published IOService object before clients attach.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn getResources(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An IOReturn code; `kIOReturnSuccess` is necessary for the IOService object to be successfully used, otherwise the registration process for the object is halted.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method is called during the registration process for an IOService object if there are successful driver matches, before any clients attach. It allows for lazy allocation of resources to an IOService object when a matching driver is found.

# getResourceService

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns a pointer to the IOResources service.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static IOService * getResourceService(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A pointer to the IOResources instance. It should not be released by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

IOService maintains a resource service IOResources that allows objects to be published and found globally in the I/O Kit based on a name, using the standard IOService matching and notification calls.

# getServiceRoot

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns a pointer to the root of the service plane.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static IOService * getServiceRoot(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A pointer to the IOService instance at the root of the service plane. It should not be released by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method provides an accessor to the root of the service plane for the computer.

# Document: getState

Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810137-getstate

# getState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Accessor for IOService state bits, not normally needed or used outside IOService.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOOptionBits getState(
 void ) const; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

State bits for the IOService, eg. `kIOServiceInactiveState`, `kIOServiceRegisteredState`.

# Document: getWorkLoop

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810145-getworkloop
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810145-getworkloop

# getWorkLoop

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Returns the current work loop or `provider->getWorkLoop`.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOWorkLoop * getWorkLoop() const; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A work loop, either the current work loop or it walks up the getProvider chain calling `getWorkLoop`. Eventually it will reach a valid work loop-based driver or the root of the I/O tree, where it will return a system-wide work loop. Returns 0 if it fails to find (or create) a work loop.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This function returns a valid work loop that a client can use to add an IOCommandGate to. The intention is that an IOService client has data that needs to be protected but doesn't want to pay the cost of a dedicated thread. This data has to be accessed from a provider's call-out context as well. So to achieve both of these goals the client creates an IOCommandGate to lock access to his data but he registers it with the provider's work loop, i.e. the work loop which will make the completion call-outs. This avoids a potential deadlock because the work loop gate uses a recursive lock, which allows the same lock to be held multiple times by a single thread.

# Document: handleClose

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810153-handleclose
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810153-handleclose

# handleClose

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Controls the open / close behavior of an IOService object (overrideable by subclasses).

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void handleClose(
 IOService *forClient, 
 IOOptionBitsoptions ); 
```

## Parameters

- `forClient`: Designates the client of the provider requesting the close.
- `options`: Options for the close, may be interpreted by the implementor of handleOpen.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

IOService calls this method in its subclasses in response to the close method, so the subclass may implement the request. The default implementation provides single owner access to an IOService object via open. The object is locked via lockForArbitration before `handleClose` is called.

# Document: handleIsOpen

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810164-handleisopen
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810164-handleisopen

# handleIsOpen

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Controls the open / close behavior of an IOService object (overrideable by subclasses).

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool handleIsOpen(
 const IOService *forClient ) const; 
```

## Parameters

- `forClient`: If non-zero, `isOpen` returns the open state for that client. If zero is passed, `isOpen` returns the open state for all clients.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if the specific, or any, client has the IOService object open.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

IOService calls this method in its subclasses in response to the open method, so the subclass may implement the request. The default implementation provides single owner access to an IOService object via open. The object is locked via lockForArbitration before `handleIsOpen` is called.

# Document: handleOpen

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810174-handleopen
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810174-handleopen

# handleOpen

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Controls the open / close behavior of an IOService object (overrideable by subclasses).

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool handleOpen(
 IOService *forClient, 
 IOOptionBits options, 
 void *arg ); 
```

## Parameters

- `forClient`: Designates the client of the provider requesting the open.
- `options`: Options for the open, may be interpreted by the implementor of `handleOpen`.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true`if the open was successful; `false` otherwise.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

IOService calls this method in its subclasses in response to the open method, so the subclass may implement the request. The default implementation provides single owner access to an IOService object via `open`. The object is locked via lockForArbitration before `handleOpen` is called.

# Document: initialPowerStateForDomainState

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810182-initialpowerstatefordomainstate
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810182-initialpowerstatefordomainstate

# initialPowerStateForDomainState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Determines which power state a device is in, given the current power domain state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual unsigned long initialPowerStateForDomainState(
 IOPMPowerFlagsdomainState ); 
```

## Parameters

- `domainState`: Flags that describe the character of "domain power"; they represent the `outputPowerCharacter` field of a state in the power domain's power state array.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A state number.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Power management calls this method once, when the driver is initializing power management. Most drivers do not need to implement this method, and can rely upon the default IOService implementation. The IOService implementation scans the power state array looking for the highest state whose `inputPowerRequirement` field exactly matches the value of the `domainState` parameter. If more intelligent determination is required, the power managed driver should implement the method and override the superclass's implementation.

# Document: isInactive

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810198-isinactive
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810198-isinactive

# isInactive

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Checks if the IOService object has been terminated, and is in the process of being destroyed.

## Declaration

```objectivec
bool isInactive(
 void ) const; 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if the IOService object has been terminated.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

When an IOService object is successfully terminated, it is immediately made inactive, which blocks further attach()es, matching or notifications occuring on the object. It remains inactive until the last client closes, and is then finalized and destroyed.

# isOpen

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Determines whether a specific, or any, client has an IOService object open.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool isOpen(
 const IOService *forClient = 0 ) const; 
```

## Parameters

- `forClient`: If non-zero, \<codeisOpenreturns the open state for that client. If zero is passed, \<codeisOpenreturns the open state for all clients.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

\<codetrueif the specific, or any, client has the IOService object open.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Returns the open state of an IOService object with respect to the specified client, or when it is open by any client.

# Document: joinPMtree

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810216-joinpmtree
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810216-joinpmtree

# joinPMtree

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Joins the driver into the power plane of the I/O Registry.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void joinPMtree(
 IOService *driver ); 
```

## Parameters

- `driver`: The driver to be added to the power plane, usually `this`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A driver uses this method to call its nub when initializing (usually in its `start` routine after calling PMinit), to be attached into the power management hierarchy (i.e., the power plane). A driver usually calls this method on the driver for the device that provides it power (this is frequently the nub). Before this call returns, the caller will probably be called at setPowerParent and setAggressiveness and possibly at addPowerChild as it is added to the hierarchy. This method may be overridden by a nub subclass.

# Document: lockForArbitration

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810228-lockforarbitration
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810228-lockforarbitration

# lockForArbitration

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Locks an IOService object against changes in state or ownership.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool lockForArbitration(
 bool isSuccessRequired = true ); 
```

## Parameters

- `isSuccessRequired`: If a request for access to an IOService object should be denied if it is terminated, pass `false`, otherwise pass `true`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

The registration, termination and open / close functions of IOService use `lockForArbtration` to single-thread access to an IOService object. `lockForArbitration` grants recursive access to the same thread.

# Document: makeUsable

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810246-makeusable
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810246-makeusable

# makeUsable

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Requests that a device become usable.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IOReturn makeUsable(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A return code that can be ignored by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method is called when some client of a device (or the device's own driver) is asking for the device to become usable. Power management responds by telling the object upon which this method is called to change to its highest power state. `makeUsable` is implemented using changePowerStateToPriv. Subsequent requests for lower power, such as from `changePowerStateToPriv`, will pre-empt this request.

# Document: mapDeviceMemoryWithIndex

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810261-mapdevicememorywithindex
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810261-mapdevicememorywithindex

# mapDeviceMemoryWithIndex

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Maps a physical range of a device.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOMemoryMap * mapDeviceMemoryWithIndex(
 unsigned intindex, 
 IOOptionBits options = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `index`: An index into the array of ranges assigned to the device.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An instance of IOMemoryMap, or zero if the index is beyond the count available. The mapping should be released only when access to it is no longer required.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This method creates a mapping for the IODeviceMemory at the given index, with `IODeviceMemory::map(options)`. The mapping is represented by the returned instance of IOMemoryMap, which should not be released until the mapping is no longer required.

# matchLocation

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Allows a registered IOService object to direct location matching.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOService * matchLocation(
 IOService *client ); 
```

## Parameters

- `client`: The IOService object at which matching is taking place.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Returns the IOService instance to be used for location matching.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

By default, a location matching property will be applied to an IOService object's provider. This method allows that behavior to be overridden by families.

# Document: matchPropertyTable

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810286-matchpropertytable
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810286-matchpropertytable

# matchPropertyTable

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Allows a registered IOService object to implement family specific matching.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool matchPropertyTable(
 OSDictionary *table, 
 SInt32 *score ); 
```

## Parameters

- `table`: The dictionary of properties to be matched against.
- `score`: Pointer to the current driver's probe score, which is used to order multiple matching drivers in the same match category. It defaults to the value of the `IOProbeScore` property in the drivers property table, or `kIODefaultProbeScore` if none is specified.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`false` if the family considers the matching dictionary does not match in properties it understands; `true` otherwise.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

All matching on an IOService object will call this method to allow a family writer to implement matching in addition to the generic methods provided by IOService. The implementer should examine the matching dictionary passed to see if it contains properties the family understands for matching, and use them to match with the IOService object if so. Note that since matching is also carried out by other parts of the I/O Kit, the matching dictionary may contain properties the family does not understand - these should not be considered matching failures.

# Document: maxCapabilityForDomainState

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810302-maxcapabilityfordomainstate
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810302-maxcapabilityfordomainstate

# maxCapabilityForDomainState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Determines a driver's highest power state possible for a given power domain state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual unsigned long maxCapabilityForDomainState(
 IOPMPowerFlagsdomainState ); 
```

## Parameters

- `domainState`: Flags that describe the character of "domain power"; they represent the `outputPowerCharacter` field of a state in the power domain's power state array.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A state number.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

This happens when the power domain is changing state and power management needs to determine which state the device is capable of in the new domain state. Most drivers do not need to implement this method, and can rely upon the default IOService implementation. The IOService implementation scans the power state array looking for the highest state whose `inputPowerRequirement` field exactly matches the value of the `domainState` parameter. If more intelligent determination is required, the driver itself should implement the method and override the superclass's implementation.

# Document: message

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810323-message
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810323-message

# message

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Receives a generic message delivered from an attached provider.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn message(
 UInt32 type,
 IOService *provider, 
 void *argument = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `type`: A type defined in `IOMessage.h` or defined by the provider family.
- `provider`: The provider from which the message originates.
- `argument`: An argument defined by the provider family, not used by IOService.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

An IOReturn code defined by the message type.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A provider may deliver messages via the `message` method to its clients informing them of state changes, such as `kIOMessageServiceIsTerminated` or `kIOMessageServiceIsSuspended`. Certain messages are defined by the I/O Kit in `IOMessage.h` while others may be family dependent. This method is implemented in the client to receive messages.

# Document: messageClient

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810334-messageclient
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810334-messageclient

# messageClient

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Sends a generic message to an attached client.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn messageClient(
 UInt32 messageType,
 OSObject *client, 
 void *messageArgument = 0,
 vm_size_t argSize = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `messageType`: A type defined in `IOMessage.h` or defined by the provider family.
- `client`: A client of the IOService to send the message.
- `messageArgument`: An argument defined by the provider family, not used by IOService.
- `argSize`: Specifies the size of messageArgument, in bytes. If argSize is non-zero, messageArgument is treated as a pointer to argSize bytes of data. If argSize is 0 (the default), messageArgument is treated as an ordinal and passed by value.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The return code from the client message call.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A provider may deliver messages via the message method to its clients informing them of state changes, such as `kIOMessageServiceIsTerminated` or `kIOMessageServiceIsSuspended`. Certain messages are defined by the I/O Kit in `IOMessage.h` while others may be family dependent. This method may be called in the provider to send a message to the specified client, which may be useful for overrides.

# Document: messageClients

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810353-messageclients
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810353-messageclients

# messageClients

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Sends a generic message to all attached clients.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn messageClients(
 UInt32 type, 
 void *argument = 0,
 vm_size_t argSize = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `type`: A type defined in `IOMessage.h` or defined by the provider family.
- `argument`: An argument defined by the provider family, not used by IOService.
- `argSize`: Specifies the size of argument, in bytes. If argSize is non-zero, argument is treated as a pointer to argSize bytes of data. If argSize is 0 (the default), argument is treated as an ordinal and passed by value.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Any non-`kIOReturnSuccess` return codes returned by the clients, or `kIOReturnSuccess` if all return `kIOReturnSuccess`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A provider may deliver messages via the message method to its clients informing them of state changes, such as `kIOMessageServiceIsTerminated` or `kIOMessageServiceIsSuspended`. Certain messages are defined by the I/O Kit in `IOMessage.h` while others may be family dependent. This method may be called in the provider to send a message to all the attached clients, via the messageClient method.

# Document: nameMatching(const char *, OSDictionary *)

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810365-namematching
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810365-namematching

# nameMatching(const char \*, OSDictionary \*)

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Creates a matching dictionary, or adds matching properties to an existing dictionary, that specify an IOService name match.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static OSDictionary * nameMatching(
 const char *name, 
 OSDictionary *table = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `name`: The service's name, as a const C string. Name matching is successful on IOService objects that respond successfully to the `IORegistryEntry::compareName` method.
- `table`: If zero, `nameMatching` creates a matching dictionary and returns a reference to it, otherwise the matching properties are added to the specified dictionary.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The matching dictionary created, or passed in, is returned on success, or zero on failure.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A very common matching criteria for IOService object is based on its name. `nameMatching` creates a matching dictionary that specifies any IOService object which responds successfully to the IORegistryEntry::compareName method. An existing dictionary may be passed in, in which case the matching properties will be added to that dictionary rather than creating a new one.

# Document: nameMatching(const OSString *, OSDictionary *)

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810383-namematching
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810383-namematching

# nameMatching(const OSString \*, OSDictionary \*)

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Creates a matching dictionary, or adds matching properties to an existing dictionary, that specify an IOService name match.

## Declaration

```objectivec
static OSDictionary * nameMatching(
 const OSString *name, 
 OSDictionary *table = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `name`: The service's name, as an OSString (which includes OSSymbol). Name matching is successful on IOService objects that respond successfully to the `IORegistryEntry::compareName` method.
- `table`: If zero, `nameMatching` creates a matching dictionary and returns a reference to it, otherwise the matching properties are added to the specified dictionary.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The matching dictionary created, or passed in, is returned on success, or zero on failure.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A very common matching criteria for IOService object is based on its name. `nameMatching` creates a matching dictionary that specifies any IOService object which responds successfully to the IORegistryEntry::compareName method. An existing dictionary may be passed in, in which case the matching properties will be added to that dictionary rather than creating a new one.

# Document: newUserClient

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810417-newuserclient
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810417-newuserclient

# newUserClient

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Creates a connection for a non kernel client.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn newUserClient(
 task_towningTask,
 void *securityID, 
 UInt32type,
 OSDictionary *handler, 
 IOUserClient **properties ); 
```

## Parameters

- `owningTask`: The Mach task of the client thread in the process of opening the user client. Note that in macOS, each process is based on a Mach task and one or more Mach threads. For more information on the composition of a Mach task and its relationship with Mach threads, see [Tasks and Threads](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/Darwin/Conceptual/KernelProgramming/Mach/Mach.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP30000905-CH209-TPXREF103).
- `securityID`: A token representing the access level for the task.
- `type`: A constant specifying the type of connection to be created, specified by the caller of [IOServiceOpen](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iokit/1514515-ioserviceopen) and interpreted only by the family.
- `handler`: An instance of an IOUserClient object to represent the connection, which will be released when the connection is closed, or zero if the connection was not opened.
- `properties`: A dictionary of additional properties for the connection.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A return code to be passed back to the caller of `IOServiceOpen`.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A non kernel client may request a connection be opened via the [IOServiceOpen](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iokit/1514515-ioserviceopen) library function, which will call this method in an IOService object. The rules and capabilities of user level clients are family dependent, and use the functions of the IOUserClient class for support. IOService's implementation returns `kIOReturnUnsupported`, so any family supporting user clients must implement this method.

# Document: nextIdleTimeout

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810435-nextidletimeout
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810435-nextidletimeout

# nextIdleTimeout

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Allows subclasses to customize idle power management behavior.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual SInt32 nextIdleTimeout(
 AbsoluteTimecurrentTime, 
 AbsoluteTimelastActivity,
 unsigned intpowerState); 
```

## Parameters

- `currentTime`: The current time
- `lastActivity`: The time of last activity on this device
- `powerState`: The device's current power state.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Returns the next time the device should idle off (in seconds, relative to the current time).

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Returns the next time that the device should idle into its next lower power state. Subclasses may override for custom idle behavior.

A power managed driver might override this method to provide a more sophisticated idle power off algorithm than the one defined by power management.

# Document: open

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810450-open
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810450-open

# open

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Requests active access to a provider.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual bool open(
 IOService *forClient, 
 IOOptionBits options = 0, 
 void *arg = 0 ); 
```

## Parameters

- `forClient`: Designates the client of the provider requesting the open.
- `options`: Options for the open. The provider family may implement options for open; IOService defines only `kIOServiceSeize` to request the device be withdrawn from its current owner.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

`true` if the open was successful; `false` otherwise.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

IOService provides generic open and close semantics to track clients of a provider that have established an active datapath. The use of `open` and close, and rules regarding ownership are family defined, and defined by the handleOpen and handleClose methods in the provider. Some families will limit access to a provider based on its open state.

# PM_Clamp_Timer_Expired

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void PM_Clamp_Timer_Expired(
```

# PMinit

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Initializes power management for a driver.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void PMinit(
 void ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

`PMinit` allocates and initializes the power management instance variables, and it should be called before accessing those variables or calling the power management methods. This method should be called inside the driver's `start` routine and must be paired with a call to PMstop. Most calls to `PMinit` are followed by calls to joinPMtree and registerPowerDriver.

# Document: PMstop

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810502-pmstop
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810502-pmstop

# PMstop

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Stop power managing the driver.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void PMstop(
 void ); 
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Removes the driver from the power plane and stop its power management. This method is synchronous against any power management method invocations (e.g. `setPowerState` or `setAggressiveness`), so when this method returns it is guaranteed those power management methods will not be entered. Driver should not call any power management methods after this call. Calling `PMstop` cleans up for the three power management initialization calls: PMinit, joinPMtree, and registerPowerDriver.

# Document: powerChangeDone

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810518-powerchangedone
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810518-powerchangedone

# powerChangeDone

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Tells a driver when a power state change is complete.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual void powerChangeDone(
 unsigned longstateNumber ); 
```

## Parameters

- `stateNumber`: The number of the state in the state array that the device has switched from.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Power management uses this method to inform a driver when a power change is completely done, when all interested parties have acknowledged the powerStateDidChangeTo call. The default implementation of this method is null; the method is meant to be overridden by subclassed power managed drivers. A driver should use this method to find out if a power change it initiated is complete.

# Document: powerOverrideOffPriv

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810533-poweroverrideoffpriv
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810533-poweroverrideoffpriv

# powerOverrideOffPriv

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Allows a driver to disable a power override.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IOReturn powerOverrideOffPriv(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A return code that can be ignored by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

When a driver has enabled an override via powerOverrideOnPriv, it can disable it again by calling this method in its superclass. Disabling the override reverts to the default algorithm for determining a device's power state. The superclass will now keep the device at the highest state required by `changePowerStateTo`, `changePowerStateToPriv`, and its children. Turning off the override will initiate a power change if the driver's desired power state is different from the maximum of the power managed driver's desire and the children's desires.

# Document: powerOverrideOnPriv

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810549-poweroverrideonpriv
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810549-poweroverrideonpriv

# powerOverrideOnPriv

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Allows a driver to ignore its children's power management requests and only use changePowerStateToPriv to define its own power state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
IOReturn powerOverrideOnPriv(
 void ); 
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A return code that can be ignored by the caller.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Power management normally keeps a device at the highest state required by its requests via changePowerStateTo, changePowerStateToPriv, and its children. However, a driver may ensure a lower power state than otherwise required by itself and its children using `powerOverrideOnPriv`. When the override is on, power management keeps the device's power state in the state specified by `changePowerStateToPriv`. Turning on the override will initiate a power change if the driver's `changePowerStateToPriv` desired power state is different from the maximum of the `changePowerStateTo` desired power state and the children's desires.

# Document: powerStateDidChangeTo

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810564-powerstatedidchangeto
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810564-powerstatedidchangeto

# powerStateDidChangeTo

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Informs interested parties that a device has changed to a different power state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual IOReturn powerStateDidChangeTo( 
 IOPMPowerFlagscapabilities, 
 unsigned longstateNumber, 
 IOService *whatDevice ); 
```

## Parameters

- `capabilities`: Flags that describe the capability of the device in the new power state (they come from the `capabilityFlags` field of the new state in the power state array).
- `stateNumber`: The number of the state in the state array that the device is switching to.
- `whatDevice`: A pointer to the driver that is changing. It can be used by a driver that is receiving power state change notifications for multiple devices to distinguish between them.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The driver returns `IOPMAckImplied` if it has prepared for the power change when it returns. If it has started preparing but not finished, it should return a number of microseconds which is an upper limit of the time it will need to finish preparing. Then, when it has completed its preparations, it should call acknowledgePowerChange.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Power management informs interested parties that a device has changed to a different power state. Interested parties are those that have registered for this notification via registerInterestedDriver. If you have called `registerInterestedDriver` on a power managed driver, you must implemnt powerStateWillChangeTo and `powerStateDidChangeTo` to receive the notifications. `powerStateDidChangeTo` is called in a clean and separate thread context. `powerStateWillChangeTo` is called before a power state transition takes place; `powerStateDidChangeTo` is called after the transition has completed.

# Document: powerStateForDomainState

Source path: documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810576-powerstatefordomainstate
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/ioservice/1810576-powerstatefordomainstate

# powerStateForDomainState

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Determines what power state the device would be in for a given power domain state.

## Declaration

```objectivec
virtual unsigned long powerStateForDomainState(
 IOPMPowerFlagsdomainState ); 
```

## Parameters

- `domainState`: Flags that describe the character of "domain power"; they represent the `outputPowerCharacter` field of a state in the power domain's power state array.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

A state number.

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Power management calls a driver with this method to find out what power state the device would be in for a given power domain state. This happens when the power domain is changing state and power management needs to determine the effect of the change. Most drivers do not need to implement this method, and can rely upon the default IOService implementation. The IOService implementation scans the power state array looking for the highest state whose `inputPowerRequirement` field exactly matches the value of the `domainState` parameter. If more intelligent determination is required, the power managed driver should implement the method and override the superclass's implementation.
